items.headline: Iran says it fired drones at a US radar in Bahrain
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say six drones targeted a US air defence radar at Bahrain's Riffa Air Base as a warning over activity in the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain says its air defences stopped several attacks.

items.headline: UK, Australia, Canada and Italy urge Israel to let aid into Gaza
items.summary: The four countries accuse Israel of blocking tents and other supplies from reaching Gaza despite the humanitarian crisis.

items.headline: Saudi-led coalition shoots down Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh
items.summary: The coalition says it intercepted two ballistic missiles and two drones. The UN migration agency says more than 340,000 Yemenis have been displaced since August as fighting escalates.

items.headline: FTSE 100 ends the week at a three-month high
items.summary: The index rose 0.4% on Friday to about 10,906, its third gain in a row, helped by oil majors such as Shell and BP as oil prices held firm.

items.headline: UK inflation and jobs figures due this week
items.summary: After strong GDP data last week, markets will watch whether price growth speeds up, which would raise the risk of another Bank of England rate rise before the year ends.

items.headline: US Treasury chief wants an outsider to run Nvidia
items.summary: Scott Bessent has called for someone from outside the company to lead Nvidia after Jensen Huang's resignation.

items.headline: Anthropic lowers its IPO valuation target to about $1.4 trillion
items.summary: That is below the roughly $2 trillion investors expected earlier this year. Pricing is set for Wednesday, with trading from Thursday; Nvidia also reports results on Tuesday.

items.headline: Nvidia investors ask board to keep door open for Huang
items.summary: Two large shareholders wrote to the board saying interim CEO Colette Kress can lead capably for now, but stopped short of demanding Huang's return.

items.headline: LangChain raises $300m for its AI agent platform
items.summary: The funding values the agent-building company at $3 billion.
